UCLA Latino Policy & Politics Institute

Neighborhood Data Explorer

Every LA County census tract by neighborhood composition, and the raw counts each foot-traffic dataset actually reports for them, year by year. Built so you can see what a dataset covers before you build on it.

← Findings: can you measure parks?

Where the neighborhoods are

2,493 tracts, classified from ACS 2018–2022. A tract is "70%+ Latino" or "70%+ non-Latino White" when that group is at least 70% of its population; everything else is mixed. Red marks are the nine June 2025 enforcement sites. Click a tract for its numbers.

Raw counts by year

One line per neighborhood type, summed across its tracts. These are the numbers as the vendor reports them — no indexing — so the scale differences between datasets are real and the caveats under each chart matter.

Scale Other / mixed is ~4x the size of 70%+ Latino, so log makes the smaller groups readable
Raw counts by year and neighborhood type

Tract classification: ACS 2018–2022 five-year estimates, 2020 tract boundaries. Enforcement sites are the nine used in the Cost of Fear analysis. Code and data: github.com/albertkun/ice-impact-replication.
